title: Harmonic calibration checker with adaptive golden sets for FP8/INT8 rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Build an automated accuracy validation harness that runs end-to-end calibration and acceptance checks for FP8/INT8 model variants before gradual rollout. Scope includes: (1) generation and maintenance of adaptive golden prompt cohorts (cohort-aware selection, rubric tagging), (2) deterministic replay + stochastic sampling of generation, (3) metric computation pipeline (logprob deltas, token-error rates, embedding similarity, instruction-following score, hallucination detectors), (4) pass/fail gating rules and automatic canary rollback triggers, and (5) integration with CI, Console dashboards, and alerting. Acceptance criteria: (A) harness produces stable pass/fail decisions for three representative customer cohorts within five runs at 95% confidence, (B) false positive rate (blocking a safe quant rollout) < 2% on historical rollouts, (C) end-to-end runtime for full validation on a standard 8-GPU dedicated pool < 90 minutes, and (D) automated rollback executed within 10 minutes of a failing canary run when configured.
steps: Define cohort taxonomy and seed golden prompts per cohort (ui/content, customer-churn, legal-docs, embeddings-heavy)
Implement adaptive golden curator: incorporate new failing examples into golden sets and retire stale prompts
Instrument calibration runner to produce layer/channel scale tables for FP8 and INT8 variants
Build metric engine that computes: token-level logprob delta vs baseline, top-k match rate, embedding cosine drift, KL over logits, and hallucination-score using reference extractors
Design gate engine: configurable thresholds (absolute & delta), weighted metric aggregation, and hysteresis to avoid flapping
Integrate with CI: nightly smoke, pre-merge validation for quantization PRs, and canary job for staged rollouts
Create Console dashboard tiles: per-cohort pass rate, metric time-series, and breakdown by model layer sensitivity
Add alerting rules: critical when drift > threshold for two consecutive runs; notify SRE+PM on PagerDuty and channel #quant-rollouts
comments: 2025-11-05 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to cohort-based golden sets and 3 core metrics (logprob delta, embedding drift, top-k match). Assigned Marco to lead engineering work.
2025-12-18 - Design review with PM/Design: agreed on cohort taxonomy and UI flags for 'sensitive' cohorts. Decided to attach cohort tags to telemetry for downstream analysis.

2026-01-09 - Prototype: implemented deterministic replay harness and baseline comparison tool. Initial runs show larger variance on conversational cohorts due to stochastic sampling; introduced temperature control in evaluation.
2026-02-02 - Trade-off discussion: lowered sample size for nightly runs to reduce cost, added stratified sampling to preserve sensitivity for rare but high-impact cohorts.
2026-02-25 - PR feedback from SRE: requested rate-limited runner and soft-quota guard to avoid noisy canary spikes during busy periods (linked below).
2026-03-04 - Integration test: calibration runner now emits per-layer scale tables for FP8 INT8 and archives artifacts to artifacts-storage; saved sample artifacts for audit.
2026-03-09 - In Review: gating rules implemented; UX for toggling hysteresis and canary size pending product feedback. Preparing runbook for manual override and rollback validation.
notes_on_metrics: Primary signal: weighted_score = 0.5*logprob_delta_norm + 0.3*embedding_cosine_drop + 0.2*instr_follow_drop. Gate passes when weighted_score < 0.015 and no individual metric exceeds its per-cohort ceiling. Secondary checks: token-coverage anomalies and KL spikes are surfaced as warnings. All numeric thresholds configurable per project and persisted with calibration checkpoint metadata.
risk_and_tradeoffs: Sensitivity vs cost: More samples increase statistical confidence but linearly increase GPU time. Calibration artifacts can mask production runtime differences if KV cache or batching behavior differs; we will flag runs that use different caching parameters. Recall sensitivity varies across cohorts; for highly critical cohorts (legal/finance) we will set stricter per-metric ceilings. Potential for noisy pass/fail due to distributional drift; plan to incorporate temporal smoothing and require consecutive failing runs before auto-rollback.
next_steps: Finalize UX for hysteresis controls, land PR for artifact retention policy, schedule canary on runtime-2.4 with 5% traffic, and run historical backtest against the last 12 quant rollouts to estimate FP/FN rates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end harness merges with green CI and interfaces with Console, 2) Backtest shows false-block rate < 2% and false-pass rate < 3% on historical rollouts, 3) Onboard two customer cohorts to run daily, 4) Runbook and SLA for rollback validated with SRE.
